claims: Admitted records use closed schemas and deterministic canonicalization.
Declared patch paths must remain within exact owned and declared paths.
Provider patch and log bytes are bounded.
limitations: CID admission generally validates shape rather than the bytes named.
Lexical path admission does not prove descriptor-rooted filesystem containment.
controls.title: Closed wire, identity, bound, and lexical scope admission

claims: The adapter registry has a closed name and option set.
Adapters cannot approve or publish their own proposal.
Publication requires the frozen lifecycle stage sequence and policy gate.
limitations: Injected port and adapter code executes before returned records are admitted.
Port claims are not a substitute for a sandbox or trust-admission proof.
controls.title: Closed adapter authority and governed lifecycle

claims: External patches require bounded strict textual unified diffs and exact declared paths.
Replay fixtures bind exact response, patch, selector, invocation, and proposal identities.
limitations: Replay admission does not establish repository tree, environment, policy generation, signer, or parent freshness.
Patch content semantics such as proof weakening are not evaluated here.
controls.title: External patch and replay fixture admission

claims: Exact executable and cwd identities, argv-only execution, and clean environment are enforced.
Linux namespaces, socket denial, write-restricting Landlock, capability drop, and process-tree cleanup are handshake gated.
Output, time, cancellation, response schema, and patch scope are bounded.
limitations: Host read confinement and hostile same-UID mutation are explicitly outside the current claim.
Codex, arbitrary adapters, tests, fixtures, apply, and verifier processes do not automatically use this boundary.
The control fails unavailable outside its supported Linux kernel and architecture prerequisites.
controls.title: CommandAdapter process sandbox

claims: Live Codex requires an explicit permit and the supported mechanism.
Requests and responses bind task, repository, context, route, model, revision, scope, and bounds.
Diagnostic output is bounded and pattern-redacted.
limitations: Installed Codex uses ordinary subprocess execution outside the verified CommandAdapter boundary.
Live environment forwarding includes HOME, CODEX_HOME, and OPENAI_API_KEY.
Network is not bound to a route-scoped endpoint allowlist and cancellation is cooperative around a blocking subprocess.
platforms: platform behavior delegated to installed Codex
controls.title: Codex permit, mechanism, identity, scope, and diagnostic admission

claims: Patch material is applied in a detached worktree and canonical HEAD is compared before and after.
Absolute, traversal, and Git-metadata paths are rejected lexically.
Failed or nonpublishing runs attempt worktree discard.
limitations: Ordinary destination path operations can follow repository symlinks.
Lifecycle gates consume port claims and do not independently prove disposable descriptor-rooted containment.
controls.title: Detached worktree, canonical-head, and lexical path checks

claims: Writer, generation, token, and idempotency keys gate checkpoint persistence.
Stale leases or fences cannot publish.
Ambiguous effectful interruption becomes repair_required rather than success.
limitations: The tested store is an in-process dictionary, not an atomic cross-process or distributed CAS proof.
Injected store records are not fully authenticated by the accelerator.
controls.title: Fenced recovery, idempotency, and ambiguity handling

claims: Live modes reject replayed, simulated, stale, unavailable, unsealed, and pseudo-CID evidence classes.
Simulation watermark and self-approval remain nonpromotable.
limitations: CID validation is generally syntactic.
Signature presence is a nonempty string rather than verification by an available signer authority.
Stage artifact identities are not universally recomputed from exact persisted bytes.
controls.title: Provenance, seal, and promotion policy

claims: Wire records forbid approval, credential, and named hidden-evaluation fields.
ContextPack carries content identities rather than source bodies.
Provider diagnostics are bounded and redacted.
limitations: Capsule identities have no enforced visible-versus-hidden projection at this boundary.
No task-specific provider payload manifest or post-proposal hidden scorer gate exists.
Pattern redaction is not proof that arbitrary secret material was never read or sent.
controls.title: Provider metadata minimization and diagnostic redaction

claims: Required installed datasets and kit authorities can fail with typed unavailable status.
Production code does not need sibling source-tree discovery.
limitations: Datasets and kit requirements default false in open_runtime options.
Missing kit persistence can fall back to a synthetic local identity.
The bootstrap verification port emits a success marker without executing tests.
controls.title: Installed-authority availability checks

claims: Enforce disposable worktrees, protected-ref denial, descriptor-rooted paths, executable allowlists, resource limits, cleanup, network policy, credential stripping, and redaction.
Unsupported platform capability produces typed unavailable.
limitations: No qualification credit until authoritative adapter, test, apply, and verification paths demonstrably invoke it.
controls.title: Sandbox enforcement

claims: Verify exact bytes, CID, schema, producer, repository, tree, environment, policy, generation, parents, signature authority, and live provenance before reuse or publication.
limitations: Missing signer or canonical authority remains unavailable and no-go.
controls.title: Receipt, proof-cache, and seal trust admission

claims: Exercise out-of-scope change, required-test deletion, proof weakening, prompt injection, command injection, policy edits, authority claims, and response scope lies in disposable fixtures.
limitations: This task cannot repair runtime failures; failures reopen the owning implementation task.
controls.title: Patch and agent adversarial tests

claims: Separate visible and hidden projections, deny future answers and paths, minimize provider disclosure, and audit every payload.
limitations: No qualification credit until the accelerator/provider path consumes the admitted visible projection.
controls.title: Hidden benchmark and provider-disclosure isolation

claims: Exercise stale and ABA writers, duplicate results, crashes, ambiguous effects, idempotence, and cleanup across integrated security boundaries.
limitations: Tests cannot repair runtime or storage failures and must preserve failing schedules.
controls.title: Concurrency and interruption adversarial integration

claims: Reconcile every frozen threat against immutable PCCE-071 through PCCE-075 evidence and issue explicit qualification or no-go.
limitations: The gate cannot repair controls, waive unavailable tests, or act as a preventive runtime control.
controls.title: Security evidence audit and qualification gate

qualification_policy.effective_control_rule: Only exact observed code and test evidence can receive limited credit within its declared boundary.

residual_risks.description: Source semantics can influence an agent without enforced instruction/data separation or semantic policy invariants.
Tests, Codex, and arbitrary adapters are outside the tested CommandAdapter process boundary.
Live Codex has broad network and credential-bearing environment access.
Lexical worktree path checks do not prove symlink-safe descriptor-rooted containment.
Receipt, seal, signature, parent, environment, and transitive byte trust is incomplete.
Hidden benchmark and least-disclosure provider projections are absent.
In-process fencing does not prove cross-process CAS atomicity or ABA safety.
Interruption cleanup is not proven across every process and lifecycle stage.
Optional authorities, synthetic persistence, and marker-only verification can overstate evidence.
New security modules can exist without authoritative runtime call-path integration.

assumptions: the reviewed source snapshot is immutable
unavailable or unintegrated security evidence is a no-go
out_of_scope: runtime repair or security qualification in PCCE-070

threats.attack_summary: Repository text attempts to redirect policy, expand scope, weaken checks, or induce disclosure.
threats.code_owner: accelerator context, adapter, and lifecycle owners

impact.description: Can disclose context or host data and corrupt patch or qualification decisions.

preconditions: An admitted source capsule or repository body is dereferenced into agent-visible context.
The agent or provider interprets untrusted source text alongside governing instructions.
threats.title: Untrusted repository and source prompt injection

threats.attack_summary: A test or fixture attempts host escape, credential access, unbounded execution, false success, or escaped mutation.

impact.description: Can compromise host confidentiality, evidence integrity, and execution availability.

preconditions: A verifier executes attacker-controlled test or fixture setup code.
The execution path has host, process, network, or publication authority not denied by an integrated sandbox.
threats.title: Malicious tests and fixtures

threats.attack_summary: A proposal lies about scope, deletes required tests, weakens proofs, or edits governing policy while appearing structurally valid.
threats.code_owner: accelerator adapter, lifecycle, and policy owners

impact.description: Can corrupt the canonical code and falsely satisfy verification or proof obligations.

preconditions: An untrusted agent or external actor can submit a patch within an admitted task.
Sensitive tests, proofs, or policies may be inside declared ownership without a semantic invariant.
threats.title: Untrusted agent patch and policy weakening

threats.attack_summary: A lexical in-scope path resolves outside the disposable worktree or mutates protected metadata.
threats.code_owner: accelerator scope, worktree, and sandbox owners

impact.description: Can read or mutate host and canonical repository paths.

preconditions: A patch or repository layout supplies traversal, absolute, symlink, metadata, or race-sensitive paths.
A consumer resolves the path without a descriptor-rooted containment proof.
threats.title: Scope and path escape

threats.attack_summary: A process escapes limits, inherits authority, leaves descendants, or injects shell or argument behavior.
threats.code_owner: accelerator command, adapter, verifier, and sandbox owners

impact.description: Can compromise the host or deny service beyond the task boundary.

preconditions: An executable, adapter, test, or descendant process starts with unintended host authority.
The relevant execution path is not covered by verified kernel and cleanup controls.
threats.title: Process and command escape

threats.attack_summary: A child bypasses deny-by-default policy to exfiltrate data or reach unintended services.

impact.description: Can disclose host or context data and invoke unauthorized external effects.

preconditions: A live child or provider transport can create internet, loopback, or Unix-socket channels.
No exact route-scoped endpoint decision constrains the live network path.
threats.title: Network escape

threats.attack_summary: Sensitive material is inherited, read, sent, or retained in diagnostics or evidence.
threats.code_owner: accelerator adapter, output, and sandbox owners

impact.description: Can disclose credentials and enable follow-on unauthorized access.

preconditions: A parent environment, configuration directory, readable host path, request, response, or log contains sensitive material.
The child or provider path can read or transmit it.
threats.title: Secret and credential escape

threats.attack_summary: Forged evidence is admitted into reuse, sealing, publication, or qualification.
threats.code_owner: accelerator policy/lifecycle and kit trust owners

impact.description: Can produce false proof and release claims.

preconditions: An evidence producer supplies a plausible schema, CID, signature string, status, or seal identity.
The consumer does not verify exact bytes and authority-bound provenance transitively.
threats.title: Evidence, receipt, and seal forgery

threats.attack_summary: Stale, poisoned, simulated, corrupt, or wrong-parent evidence is reused as current.
threats.code_owner: accelerator replay/recovery and kit trust owners

impact.description: Can corrupt proof reuse and cause stale or duplicate publication.

preconditions: Previously valid or corrupt material is available under another tree, environment, policy, parent, or generation.
A selector or cache lookup does not validate the complete live trust tuple.
threats.title: Replay, stale cache, poisoning, and wrong parent

threats.attack_summary: An agent or provider observes hidden tests, answers, future patches, or scorer evidence.
preconditions: Hidden or future evaluation material shares a namespace, projection, path, log, or provider payload with pre-proposal context.
The scorer is reachable before proposal closure.
threats.title: Hidden benchmark and future-answer leakage

threats.attack_summary: A provider receives unnecessary repository, hidden evaluation, or host-related information.
threats.code_owner: accelerator adapter and datasets benchmark owners

impact.description: Can disclose protected context and invalidate evaluation isolation.

preconditions: A provider request is built without a task-specific visible-data manifest.
Capsule identities, paths, diagnostics, or other context exceed the declared access policy.
threats.title: Provider over-disclosure

threats.attack_summary: A stale, ABA, or duplicate writer persists or publishes inconsistent state.
threats.code_owner: accelerator recovery and kit CAS owners

impact.description: Can produce duplicate, stale, or corrupt evidence and deadlock progress.

preconditions: Two or more workers share a canonical root, worktree parent, lease, generation, checkpoint store, or publication target.
An operation races validation, apply, persistence, or publication.
threats.title: Concurrent mutation, stale or ABA writer, and duplicate result

threats.attack_summary: An ambiguous effect is repeated, mislabeled success, or leaves live processes, worktrees, or storage state.
threats.code_owner: accelerator process, lifecycle, and recovery owners

impact.description: Can falsely accept partial work or leak persistent execution effects.

preconditions: Cancellation, timeout, crash, or process death occurs during apply, check, proof, seal, provider invocation, or publication.
The durable record cannot prove whether the effect completed.
threats.title: Interruption and ambiguous terminal execution

threats.attack_summary: The component lies about scope or authority, mutates state, reads secrets, opens network, or leaves descendants before returning a rejected result.
threats.code_owner: accelerator registry, adapter, sandbox, lifecycle, and recovery owners

impact.description: Can compromise every host and evidence boundary despite later output rejection.

preconditions: An admitted registry adapter, injected transport, or executable is compromised.
It executes before returned records are checked for identity, scope, provenance, or authority.
threats.title: Compromised adapter or transport
